text:
maria: quick Q — noticed behavior in the model-selection endpoint during a canary. I passed `model_ids: [\"redwood-alpaca-13b\", \"rw-7b-quant\"]` + `route_hints: { region: \"eu\", tier: \"standard\" }` but response shows served_model=rw-7b-quant even though eu/standard should prefer redwood-alpaca-13b. is that expected?

kevin: short answer: possibly. fallbacks can change the final served model if capacity or compatibility constraints hit. can you paste the request payload + response?

maria: pasted minimal example below — this was from a private canary around 09:10 UTC
```json
{
  "model_select": ["redwood-alpaca-13b","rw-7b-quant"],
  "route_hints": {"region":"eu","tier":"standard"},
  "max_tokens": 256
}
```
response headers included `x-served-model: rw-7b-quant` and body had `served_model: \"rw-7b-quant\"` (no mention of original requested model).

lina: a couple of things to check — 1) if redwood-alpaca-13b wasn't available in the chosen region/tier, the router will pick the highest-priority compatible model; 2) the API contract currently returns `served_model` (single canonical name) not the full request list. that was intended so clients can know what was used.

sanjay: that second bit matters for backward compat. older clients expected `model` in the response and sometimes parsed `model` assuming "the same as the input". we added `served_model` because of async routing, but we should check whether we need to also echo `requested_models` for audit.

kevin: agreed. proposal: API returns both `served_model` and `route_decision` summary. something like:
```json
"served_model": "rw-7b-quant",
"requested_models": ["redwood-alpaca-13b","rw-7b-quant"],
"route_decision": {"reason": "capacity_unavailable","fallback_to": "rw-7b-quant","region":"eu","tier":"standard"}
```
This keeps backward compat (served_model) and gives transparency.

maria: sounds good. small note: for privacy/compliance when Private customers use VPC-only models, we should not leak internal pool IDs in `route_decision`. keep it high level (`reason` enum + model id allowed).

oliver: +1. also we should document whether `route_hints` is a hard requirement vs soft preference. current behavior: `route_hints` are hints (soft) and only strict when `route_mode: hard` is set. maybe we need explicit `route_mode` param to avoid surprises.

sanjay: yep — add `route_mode: ["preferred" (default), "strict"]`. when strict and region/tier unavailable, return 409 + explainable error rather than silently fallback. that keeps clients safe.

kevin: implementation note for eng-runtime: will need a small API-contract migration PR + tests. I'll  put up a draft and tag reviewers. action items: @kevin to draft PR for response fields + route_mode, @lina to update docs/compat notes, @maria to capture canary logs and add one failing example to the PR.

deploy-bot: deploy queued for branch:feature/route-decision-response — CI passed. :rocket:

maria: thanks — i'll attach the canary trace and small reproducer in the PR. tagging folks so this is async-friendly. :slightly_smiling_face:
